newsitem.title: UK: UK water customer group warns on clean-up costs.
newsitem.headline: UK water customer group warns on clean-up costs.

text.p: A UK water industry consumer group has advised European members of parliament (MEPs) that clean-up proposals on beaches from Brussels could cost as much as 4.2 billion stg to implement.

In a briefing note to MEPs, the National Customer Council (ONCC) of water watchdog Ofwat said proposals from the European Commission on bathing waters may "involve significant capital expenditure" of between 2.5 and 4.2 billion stg in the UK.

The ONCC said it was not opposed to improvements suggested but that "a proper balance must be struck between environmental and public health considerations and the interest of consumers in relation to costs and affordability."
It said the predicted costs would result in an increase of between eight stg and 14 stg on current average household sewerage bills.
"For some water companies with extensive coastal areas the increase could be twice the national average," the ONCC added.
